sections.h2: What must a landlord do with tenant money when selling a rented house in Florida?
sections.html:
Section 83.49(7) requires the seller to hand all security deposits and advance rents to the new owner, with earned interest and an accurate accounting for each tenant account. The transfer is the landlord's job at the time of sale, so build it into the closing checklist.

Once the funds and records move and the new owner or agent signs a written receipt, the seller is released from the duty to hold that money. A new owner is presumed to have received the deposit from the previous owner, but that presumption stops at one month's rent. A buyer who skips the transfer can end up facing a tenant's refund claim for money it never saw.

Deposits have their own rules while held. The landlord keeps the money in a Florida account for the tenant's benefit, or posts a surety bond with the circuit court clerk, and must give written notice of how it is held within 30 days of receiving it. Landlords renting fewer than five units are excused from that notice, though not from holding the funds properly.

Timing at move-out matters too. A landlord making no claim must refund the deposit inside 15 days of the tenancy's end. One who wants to keep part must send a written claim by certified mail or e-mail inside 30 days, and the tenant gets 15 days to object. A buyer who inherits a tenancy inherits these clocks, so ask the seller for the full ledger.

  • Each tenant's deposit and advance rent amount.
  • Where the money is held and any interest earned.
  • The date each lease began and any renewal, since a renewal counts as a new rental agreement and carries the deposit forward as new.
  • A copy of each signed lease and the written notice that told the tenant how the deposit is held.
  • The name and mailing address of whoever will take over notices and rent after closing.

sections.h2: Can a tenant be forced out so the house can be sold empty?
sections.html:
Only through the notices and court steps in Chapter 83. The statute does not list a planned sale as a reason to end a lease early, so read the lease term first and match it to the right notice period.

Section 83.57 sets the notice to end a periodic tenancy, measured before the end of the rental period.

  • Monthly tenancy: 30 days or more.
  • Yearly tenancy: 60 days or more.
  • Quarterly tenancy: 30 days or more.
  • Weekly tenancy: 7 days or more.

A tenant with a fixed-term lease generally stays through the term unless the lease or the statute provides a ground to end it. Have a Florida landlord-tenant attorney read the lease before any buyer is told the keys will be handed over empty.

sections.h2: What notices apply if the tenant is behind or breaking the lease?
sections.html:
Nonpayment gets a 3-day notice under section 83.56(3), counted without Saturdays, Sundays or court-observed holidays. The notice demands the rent or possession.

Other violations are split into two kinds. For a curable violation, the tenant has 7 days after delivery to fix it. For an incurable one, such as intentional damage to the property or continued unreasonable disturbance, the notice gives 7 days to vacate. A repeat of the same violation within 12 months lets the landlord sue without new notice.

Delivery can be by mail, handing over a true copy, e-mail under section 83.505, or leaving a copy at the residence when the tenant is absent. A lease cannot waive these notice requirements. If the landlord accepts partial rent after serving a 3-day notice, the landlord must give a receipt with the balance due, pay that rent into the court registry when filing, or serve a new notice.

sections.h2: What happens in court after a notice runs out?
sections.html:
Suit is filed, the tenant gets a short window to pay rent into the registry, and a sheriff carries out any judgment.

Under section 83.60(2), a tenant who raises any defense other than payment must pay accrued rent into the court registry, or file a motion to determine rent, within 5 days after service, again excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays. A tenant who misses that step waives the defenses and the landlord gets an immediate default judgment.

After judgment, the clerk issues a writ to the sheriff, who puts the landlord back in possession after 24 hours' conspicuously posted notice. Under section 83.62 weekends and holidays do not stop that 24-hour clock. Build the listing timeline around these steps, because each one adds days.

sections.h2: What does the landlord owe the tenant before and after the sale?
sections.html:
Chapter 83 has the landlord identify, in writing and by the first day of the tenancy, who the landlord or the authorized notice recipient is, with a street address. Section 83.50 says that person keeps the authority until the tenant is told otherwise.

After a sale, tenants need to know where to send rent and notices. Have the closing attorney draft a written notice naming the new owner or agent, delivered to the tenant's residence or by e-mail under section 83.505.

sections.h2: What taxes and costs should a landlord-seller expect?
sections.html:
A landlord-seller pays the same deed tax as any seller, and the rental status changes how the property tax bill behaves. Section 201.02 sets deed tax at 70 cents per $100, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded.

Rental property has no homestead protection. Its assessed value is limited to a 10 percent annual increase, and the buyer starts at just value after the transfer. The tax collector mails bills in November, and the state calendar lists early-payment discounts that shrink each month through February.

A house that was once the owner's home and is now rented has lost its exemption, because renting ends homestead. Ask the county property appraiser to confirm the roll and the tax collector for the payoff before closing.

faqs.q: What happens to my tenant's security deposit when I sell?
faqs.a: Transfer it. Section 83.49(7) requires the seller to pass the deposits and advance rents to the new owner with earned interest and an accounting for each tenant. Get a written receipt, and the seller is released from holding the money.

faqs.q: What notice ends a monthly tenancy?
faqs.a: Thirty days or more before a monthly period ends, per section 83.57. Year-to-year tenancies need 60 days, quarter-to-quarter 30 days and week-to-week 7 days.

faqs.q: Can I evict a tenant just because I am selling?
faqs.a: Not on that ground alone. You need a legal basis from Chapter 83, such as a properly served nonpayment or violation notice or the end of a periodic tenancy. Check your lease term with a Florida attorney.

faqs.q: How long does the 3-day notice for unpaid rent last?
faqs.a: Three days, not counting Saturdays, Sundays or court-observed legal holidays, under section 83.56(3). It demands payment or possession and can be delivered by mail, hand, e-mail or posting at the home if the tenant is absent.

faqs.q: Who tells the tenant where to send rent after a sale?
faqs.a: The landlord, or the person authorized to receive notices, must tell the tenant in writing who to contact. The authorization stays in place under section 83.50 until the tenant hears otherwise, so a new-owner letter belongs in the closing packet.
